                      LARRY AND DONNA MARTIN’S INITIAL BRIEF
                           LINK J24, PARCEL NUMBER 1350

          Pursuant to State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) Order Nos. 6 and 32, Larry

  and Donna Martin (the Martins) timely file this Initial Brief on June 19, 2026.


                                   I.   EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

         The Martins oppose any route that contains Link J24. This brief will address the following

  facts about Link J24:


                Link J24 is not on Route 894, the “best meets” route and is not included in the

                 Applicants’ top six routes;

                Link J24 is not on Staff’s recommended Routes 547 or 296;

                Link J24 is not in any expert’s routing recommendation;

                Any route that uses J24 is more expensive than an equivalent route using J27;

                The Environmental Assessment (EA) significantly overstates the length that J24

                 parallels actual property boundaries;
                                                                                                           Page 2 of 7



                 Link J24 would be visible from Colorado Bend State Park;

                 Utilizing Link J24 requires crossing the Colorado River through undisturbed land

                  (Link J22 or J26) at a location that has already been rejected by this Commission

                  in the past;

                 Link J24 has at least one confirmed historical site that contained Native American

                  remains within the right-of-way;

                  At least one landowner who owns property on both J24 and J27 would prefer J27

                  if one of those two links is used;

                 Link J24 forms a “V” less than 1,000 feet from a residence, adding three turning

                  structures; and

                 Link J24 together with J25 have more habitable structures than Link J27.

        For these reasons, any route utilizing Link J24 should not be selected.


                          II.    EXPERT ROUTING RECOMMENDATIONS

        Of the thousands of routing options provided in this docket, the recommendations of the

Applicants and every routing expert exclude J24 from consideration in their top routes. Applicants’
                                                                 1                                                  2
best meets route uses Links J22 and J27, and not J24. Applicants’ top six routes do not use J24.

When crossing the Colorado River, Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) Staff’s
                                                                                     3
(Staff’s) route uses J11, and Staff’s second choice route uses Link J31. Cherokee Creek Partners




        1
            Oncor & LCRA TSC Ex. 1 (Application) Attachment No. 11, at 5.
        2
           Link N3 Opposition Landowners Ex. 12 (Oncor and LCRA TSC Response to Hodge and Schwertner Farms
First RFI 1-17).
        3
            Staff Ex. 1 (Direct Testimony of John Poole) at 19:18-20; Tr. at 91-92 (Poole Cross) (Jun. 10, 2026).
                                                                                                            Page 3 of 7



                      4                                              5
Route G uses J31. Brady Creek and Wulff Bluff use U3. Of the parties unimpacted by the “best
                                                                                 6
meets” route, none of them advocate for a route that includes J24.”

         Although no other party’s expert discussed in detail why Link J24 should not be used, there

are several reasons that make it stand out as a poor choice. It is an expensive link that includes

numerous angle structures. Three angle structures are included on Link J24 simply to move the
                                                                                                                     7
line more than 500 feet away from a home, yet the line then surrounds the home on three sides.

In an attempt to mitigate the impact to the home, the landowners proposed a modification, which

Applicants indicated is not constructable due to existing oil and gas infrastructure as well as
                            8
unnoticed landowners.


                                                  III.     COST

         Link J24 is the more expensive alternative if routing were through the central Colorado

River crossing. Evaluating the cost of the routing options in isolation from the routes as a whole,

requires simple comparison calculations.

    A. If the river is crossed at J22, two paths exist to reach the intersection of J27 and J25, where

         the lines continue to the west. The first path is J23 + J24 + J25. The second path is J23 +




         4
             Cherokee Creek Partners Ex. 1 (Direct Testimony of RaeLynn Schneider Reineke) at 11:28.
         5
             Brady Creek Intervenors Ex. 4 (Direct Testimony of Mark Turnbough) at 10:20.
         6
         See, e.g. Yates Keith Alliance Ex. 5 (Direct Testimony of Mark Anderson); Hodge-Schwertner Ex. 1 (Direct
Testimony of Brian Andrews).
         7
           The home is not a numbered or listed habitable structure because it is more than 520 feet away from the
centerline of Link J24. It is inside parcel number 1369 and adjacent to the structure labeled as parcel 1370, and it is
the home on the property of JG Wilson Sisters Ranch.
         8
             Larry Martin Ex. 3 (Oncor/LCRA Response to Wilson Sisters First RFI).
                                                                                                Page 4 of 7



       J27. Using the Applicants’ chart of costs per link, J23 + J24 + J25 = $86,437,000 while
                                         9
       J23 + J27 = $85,924,000.


   B. If the river is crossed at J26, the paths to continue west are either J24 + J25 or only J27.

       Using the Applicants’ chart of costs per link, J24 + J25 = $81,681,000. The cost of J27
                                    10
       alone is $81,168,000.


                              IV.        PARALLELING PROPERTY LINES

       In the Application, the Applicants provided an estimate of the length of paralleling

compatible rights-of way, including paralleling apparent property lines. For J24, Applicants stated
                                                          11
that property lines were paralleled for 8.43 miles. After reviewing the property tax records, which

establish that the same people own several tracts, the actual length of the property boundaries
                                                               12
paralleled on Link J24 is approximately 2.78 miles.

       Commission rules require consideration of whether the routes parallel “property lines,” not
                             13
apparent property lines.          Although Applicants have used apparent property lines as a substitute

for actual property lines in their Application, when actual property line data is available and

presented, it is the better evidence of the applicable factor in the rules. Because Link J24 only

parallels actual property boundaries for only 2.78 miles of its length, it is a poor choice.

            Link R1 Opposition Landowners Ex. 7 (Applicants’ Response to M31 RFI 1-05).
       10
            Id.
       11

       12
            Id. at 14:1-6.
       13

                        V.     AESTHETICS AND PARKS AND RECREATION

        In this particular docket, aesthetics and parks and recreation are linked. Five links impact

Post Oak State Park and Colorado Bend State Park – J22, J26, J24, J27, and J11. The Texas Parks

and Wildlife Department (TPWD) indicated a strong preference for not routing the line close to
                   14
the state parks.


                                         VI.      HISTORICAL SITES

        Link J24 contains several historical sites, as Mary Weahkee of the Comanche Nation

testified, she identified a burial mound along with a possible Spanish mine in which Comanche
                                                            15
human remains were identified in the mine shaft.                 At the hearing, Ms. Weahkee identified that
                                            16
property as Larry Martin’s property.             Mr. Martin also testified regarding these historical sites on
                                                                                            17
his property, and that the Spanish mine is within the right-of-way on Link J24.                  These known and

recognized historical sites are another reason not to utilize Link J24.


                                 VII.      LANDOWNER PREFERENCE

        Although not specifically enumerated in the rules, landowner preference is often given

consideration. For example, the standard ordering paragraphs in Certificate of Convenience and

Necessity (CCN) cases usually contain a paragraph requiring the utility to cooperate with




        14
             Oncor/LCRA Ex. 1 (Application) at Ex. F, TPWD Input on Initial Proposed Link J2 at A-893.
        15
             Comanche Nation Ex. 2 (Direct Testimony of M. Weahkee) at 7.
        16
             Tr. at 234:l-16 (Weahkee Cross) (Jun. 12, 2026).
        17
             Larry and Donna Martin Ex. 1 (Direct Testimony of L. Martin ) at 14:12–15:16
                                                                                                      Page 6 of 7



                                                                           18
landowners to implement minor deviations in the approved route.                 In this case, the JG & Wilson

Sisters Ranch own property that spans Links J24 and J27. While they oppose the use of either
                                                                                                           19
Link J24 or J27, they have explicitly stated their preference for using Link J27 over Link J24.                 If

the administrative law judges recommend or the Commission chooses a central route, the

preference of these landowners, who are impacted by both links, should be considered and given

great weight.


                                        VIII.      CONCLUSION

        Link J24 should not be used in routing the transmission line in this docket. It is not

recommended by any experts, it is expensive compared to other options, it does not parallel

property lines or any other appropriate corridor for much of its length, it is within view of Colorado

Bend State Park, and would mar the views from that park, it has known historical sites, more

habitable structures than Link J27, and would be the last choice of the Wilson landowners who

own property both on J24 and J27.

        If a route is ultimately chosen in this case, the Martins respectfully request that a route not

utilizing Link J24 be approved and any and all other relief to which they are justly entitled.

First RFI) at 4.
